title: The Indian Labour Conference: where Government, employers and unions meet
author: Editorial Desk
summary: A tripartite forum that has shaped wage policy for decades.
body:
The **Indian Labour Conference (ILC)** is the Government's tripartite consultative body on labour. Government, employers' organisations and central trade unions sit together to discuss questions of labour policy. It is held at the call of the Labour Ministry and takes its name from the same idea as the ILO's tripartism.

## Why it matters

Several of the foundational principles of labour policy came from the Conference:

- The **15th session (1957)** laid down norms for a need-based minimum wage, which unions still cite.
- The **45th session (2013)** recommended that scheme workers be treated as workers, a recommendation unions still cite.
- Later, the Government has consulted unions at the **Standing Labour Committee**, in tripartite meetings and in pre-legislative consultations.

## BMS and tripartism

BMS has regularly argued that labour laws should be made after tripartite consultation, and that the consensus reached in the Conference should be respected. It has also asked that the Conference meet regularly.

## For readers

If a headline says "Government consults unions", check which forum it refers to and who attended. A meeting with a few unions is different from a full tripartite session.
